title: Modalpartikeln
explainer_md:
Modalpartikeln are the small unstressed words that give a German sentence its tone. They change no facts — delete them and the sentence stays true — but they colour the speaker's attitude, and German without them sounds cold and abrupt. They sit in the middle field, after the verb and the pronouns, before the new information: *Komm [[doch]] mit!*

| Partikel | Wirkung | Satztyp |
|---|---|---|
| doch | urging, mild reproach | Imperativ, Aussage |
| ja | shared knowledge, surprise | Aussage |
| mal | casual, non-binding | Imperativ |
| eben / halt | resigned *that's how it is* | Aussage |
| denn | friendly interest | Frage |

*Das ist [[ja]] toll!* signals surprise, *Mach das [[mal]]!* softens an order, *Das ist [[eben]] so* shrugs. **schon** reassures or concedes (*Das schaffst du schon*), **wohl** guesses (*Er ist wohl krank*), **eigentlich** asks in passing or reveals a hidden truth (*Eigentlich wollte ich zu Hause bleiben*).

The sentence type decides: *denn* only ever appears in questions, *mal* mainly in requests, *ja* never in a question. And do not mix the particle up with its stressed twin — *Ich komme doch mit* (particle) against *Doch, ich komme!* (contradicting a negative question).

payload.prompt: Wie alt bist du ___? (freundliches Interesse)
payload.explanation: [[denn]] makes a question sound friendly instead of like an interrogation.

payload.prompt: Komm ___ mit ins Kino! (dringliche Bitte)
payload.explanation: [[doch]] in an imperative urges someone on: Komm doch mit!

payload.prompt: Das ist ___ toll! (Überraschung)
payload.explanation: [[ja]] in a statement expresses surprise or shared knowledge.

payload.prompt: Mach ___ das Fenster auf! (locker, freundlich)
payload.explanation: [[mal]] softens an order into a casual request.

payload.prompt: Das ist ___ so — da kann man nichts machen.
payload.explanation: [[eben]] signals resignation: that is simply how things are.

payload.prompt: In welchem Satztyp steht „denn“?
payload.explanation: The particle denn only appears in questions — never in an order or a statement.

payload.prompt: Welches Wort ist in „Er ist wohl krank“ die Modalpartikel?
payload.explanation: [[wohl]] marks the sentence as a guess: I suppose he is ill.

payload.prompt: Der Bus kommt ___ später. (Der Sprecher vermutet es nur.)
payload.explanation: wohl = probably, presumably — the speaker does not know for sure.

payload.prompt: Das schaffst du ___! (Der Sprecher macht Mut.)
payload.explanation: [[schon]] as a particle reassures: don't worry, you'll manage.

payload.prompt: Wo warst du ___ so lange? (freundliche Nachfrage)
payload.explanation: denn belongs in questions and takes the edge off the enquiry.

payload.prompt: Wie spät ist es ___? (beiläufige Frage)
payload.explanation: [[eigentlich]] makes a question sound casual, almost like an afterthought.

payload.prompt: Welche Partikel benutzt man süddeutsch statt „eben“?
payload.explanation: [[halt]] and eben mean the same; halt is southern German and Austrian.

payload.prompt: Welcher Satz ist falsch?
payload.explanation: ja is never used as a particle in a question; denn and eigentlich are.

payload.prompt: Wo steht die Modalpartikel im Satz?
options: im Mittelfeld, vor der neuen Information
payload.explanation: Particles live in the middle field, behind verb and pronouns: Ich habe dir doch alles erklärt.

payload.prompt: Ruf mich ___ an, wenn du Zeit hast. (unverbindlich)
payload.explanation: mal makes the request light and non-binding — sometime, whenever.

payload.prompt: Das habe ich dir ___ gesagt! (Vorwurf: du weißt es)
payload.explanation: doch in a statement appeals to knowledge both sides share — often as a reproach.

payload.prompt: Der Zug ist ___ schon weg — das sehen wir beide.
payload.explanation: ja points to something obvious to speaker and listener alike ([[Zug]]).

payload.prompt: Welche Bedeutung hat „schon“ in „Das wird schon klappen“?
payload.explanation: Here schon is not temporal (already) but reassuring: it'll work out fine.

payload.prompt: Was drückt „eigentlich“ in „Eigentlich wollte ich zu Hause bleiben“ aus?
payload.explanation: eigentlich reveals the plan behind the facts: actually I wanted to stay in — but I didn't.

payload.prompt: In welchem Satz ist „doch“ KEINE Modalpartikel?
payload.explanation: Stressed Doch at the front contradicts a negative question; the particle is unstressed and stands inside the sentence.

payload.prompt: „Sie ist wohl krank.“ bedeutet:
options: Ich vermute, dass sie krank ist.
Ich weiß sicher, dass sie krank ist.
payload.explanation: wohl weakens the claim to an assumption — comparable to dürfte or vermutlich.

payload.prompt: Welche Wortstellung ist richtig?
payload.explanation: The particle stands in the middle field after the finite verb, never first and never last ([[anrufen]]).

payload.prompt: Welche Partikel passt NICHT in einen Imperativ?
payload.explanation: denn is restricted to questions; doch and mal are typical of imperatives.

payload.prompt: „Das ist halt so.“ klingt:
payload.explanation: halt (= eben) shrugs the matter off and belongs to spoken, southern German.

payload.prompt: Welche zwei Partikeln bedeuten fast dasselbe?
payload.explanation: eben and halt are regional twins; the other pairs differ in meaning and sentence type.

payload.prompt: Komm ___ mit, es wird bestimmt lustig! (dringliche Bitte)
payload.explanation: doch urges the listener on in an invitation.

payload.prompt: Das Wetter ist heute ___ super! (Überraschung)
payload.explanation: ja marks surprise about something both can see ([[Wetter]]).

payload.prompt: Warte ___ kurz! (locker, freundlich)
payload.explanation: mal turns an order into a light request: Warte mal kurz!

payload.prompt: Wie heißt du ___? (freundliche Frage)
payload.explanation: denn only ever appears in questions and makes them sound friendly ([[heißen]]).

payload.prompt: So ist das ___, da kann man nichts ändern. (norddeutsche Variante)
payload.explanation: eben expresses resignation; in the south people say halt instead.

payload.prompt: Er ist ___ krank, sonst wäre er gekommen. (Vermutung)
payload.explanation: wohl marks the sentence as an assumption, not a fact.

payload.prompt: Keine Sorge, die Prüfung schaffst du ___! (Zuversicht)
payload.explanation: schon reassures: you will manage it all right.

payload.prompt: Was machst du ___ am Wochenende? (beiläufiges Interesse)
payload.explanation: eigentlich adds a casual, by-the-way tone to the question.

payload.prompt: Wo bleibst du ___ so lange? (ungeduldige Frage)
payload.explanation: In a question denn carries the speaker's involvement — here impatience.

payload.prompt: Statt „eben“ sagt man in Bayern und Österreich oft ___.
payload.explanation: halt is the southern equivalent of eben: Das ist halt so.

payload.prompt: Ich habe es dir ___ erklärt, hörst du nie zu? (Vorwurf)
payload.explanation: doch appeals to knowledge the listener should already have ([[erklären]]).

payload.prompt: Schau dir das ___ an, wenn du Lust hast. (unverbindlich)
payload.explanation: mal keeps the request non-binding and informal.

payload.prompt: Du weißt ___, dass ich morgen keine Zeit habe. (gemeinsames Wissen)
payload.explanation: ja refers to information both speaker and listener already share.
In an imperative the particle follows the verb directly ([[mitkommen]]).
ja stands behind the finite verb, before the new information ([[toll]]).
mal may stand before or after the object, but always inside the sentence bracket.
eben in a statement expresses resignation.
In a W-Frage denn follows the subject pronoun.
wohl turns the statement into an assumption ([[krank]]).
The particle stands behind the pronouns and before the participle at the end.

payload.translation: What's your name, by the way?
payload.explanation: eigentlich gives the question a relaxed, by-the-way tone.

payload.translation: You'll manage the exam all right.
payload.explanation: The object opens the sentence, the verb stays second, schon reassures at the end of the middle field.

payload.translation: Give me a call later sometime.
payload.explanation: mal makes the request casual; the separable prefix an closes the sentence.
